newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Jailed Bangladesh ex-president to go home soon.
newsitem.headline: Jailed Bangladesh ex-president to go home soon.

text.p: Bangladesh's jailed former president Hossain Mohammad Ershad was granted bail by the Supreme Court on Wednesday on the last of a series of corruption charges against him and was expected to be freed soon, court officials said.
"My client is very happy. He has won the legal battle," Ershad's lawyer, Yusuf Hossain Humayun, told Reuters.
"He will be out by tomorrow (Thursday). "There are some administrative procedures which we are trying to settle."
Humayun said Ershad was granted bail in a case involving corruption charges over the purchase of defence radar.
Ershad, who seized power in a bloodless coup in 1982 and was deposed in an opposition-led people's uprising in 1990, at one time faced 19 corruption charges.
He was sentenced to 23 years' imprisonment in four cases for keeping illegal firearms and corruption.
The High Court last year quashed a 10-year sentence for the arms offences and Ershad has appealed against the other convictions.
Ershad won bail last November, and was allowed access to parliament, in what was the most sensational case against him -- the charge of killing Major-General Abul Manzur during a 1981 army mutiny.
Then-President General Ziaur Rahman, husband of former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia, was killed in the mutiny.
Ershad was then the army chief. He deposed Zia's vice-president and successor Justice Abdus Sattar in the 1982 coup.
Ershad's brother, G.M. Quader, said the former president would be staying at his house at Gulshan, a residential area of Dhaka, after his release.
Ershad, head of the Jatiya party, has been living in a special jail set up near parliament house since winning a parliamentary seat in June elections.
Jubilant Jatiya leaders and supporters gathered outside the heavily guarded jail on Wednesday on hearing the court verdict, witnesses said.
"We are waiting to take our chairman (Ershad) out," one said.
Ershad's party supported Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's Awami League to form a government following the June elections.
